key_insight: Neptuna introduces a large-scale benchmark for shock-driven compressible multiphase flows and shows that model performance depends strongly on the dataset, metric, and loss design.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps identify surrogate models and training strategies that better preserve interfaces, shocks, and spectral structure in practical multiphase flow simulation workflows.
method: Built a 2.4 TB benchmark with 2D and 3D high-fidelity datasets for bubble collapse and droplet breakup.
Compared convolutional, spectral, transformer-based, and pre-trained PDE foundation models.
Tested MSE-only training against composite losses and adaptive weighting schemes such as SoftAdapt and GradNorm.
evidence_signal: The benchmark evaluates models with pointwise, spectral, feature-focused, structural, and physics-informed metrics, and reports that composite losses improve interface preservation and spectral fidelity while SoftAdapt is the most consistent adaptive weighting method.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-specific, so gains from a given model or loss may not transfer uniformly across all multiphase flow regimes or evaluation metrics.
paper_title: Neptuna: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Benchmarking Complex Multiphase Flows
